title: Infosys Goes Live With Syngenta SAP Core for 10,000 Staff in 80 Countries
excerpt: Crop Protection Core replaces multiple ERP systems with one SAP S/4HANA platform covering research, manufacturing, supply chain, regulatory, finance and commercial operations.
body:
• Infosys has gone live with Crop Protection Core, Syngenta's global SAP S/4HANA platform for its Crop Protection business.
  • The single platform supports more than 10,000 employees across 80 countries and replaces multiple legacy ERP systems.
  • It covers research, manufacturing, supply chain, regulatory, finance and commercial functions, with AI from Infosys Topaz automating routine tasks.
  • For enterprise buyers: the go-live is a reference case for large, multi-country S/4HANA migrations delivered on SAP best practices with reduced customisation.

Infosys said it has completed the implementation and go-live of Crop Protection Core, Syngenta's global SAP S/4HANA transformation for its Crop Protection business, creating a single digital core for more than 10,000 employees in 80 countries.

The programme, delivered jointly by Infosys and Syngenta, consolidates multiple ERP environments into one platform. Infosys announced the milestone on October 27 in a release carried by PR Newswire.

What was built

Built on SAP S/4HANA, Crop Protection Core brings research, manufacturing, supply chain, regulatory, finance and commercial functions onto a unified system. Core customisations were reduced in line with SAP best practices, a choice that simplifies upgrades and support over time.

The transformation used Infosys Topaz, the company's AI-first suite built on generative and agentic AI, and Infosys Cobalt cloud offerings. Infosys said the work modernised business processes, improved data quality and created a trusted enterprise data foundation. AI tools automate routine activities and drive standardisation, while staff retain control of critical decisions.

Syngenta, headquartered in Switzerland for Crop Protection and employing more than 30,000 people in over 90 countries across the wider group, sells crop protection products to farmers worldwide. A single core gives its teams the same data and processes across markets that previously ran separate systems.

"CP Core gives our people a simpler, more reliable way to work, helping us better serve farmers across all our markets."

— Feroz Sheikh, Chief Information and Digital Officer, Syngenta

Why the delivery matters for Infosys

Large ERP replacements are among the riskiest programmes in enterprise technology. They touch finance, factories and supply chains at once, and failures are public. A completed go-live at this scale — 80 countries, six major functions, one platform — gives Infosys a current reference for manufacturing and agribusiness clients considering their own move off legacy SAP systems.

Jasmeet Singh, Infosys executive vice president and global head of manufacturing, said the go-live reflected precision and deep industry expertise, and built on a long-standing collaboration with Syngenta. Coverage in CXO Today carried the same details on scope and leadership comments.

The deal also fits the pattern in Infosys's recent results, where AI-linked work has grown as a share of revenue. Here, AI was not a separate product sale. It was embedded in the delivery and in the running platform, through Topaz.

What happens next

Neither company disclosed contract value or programme duration, and the release does not set out a second phase. The stated purpose of the new core is to serve as a scalable foundation for future innovation, with stronger governance, better visibility across the Crop Protection business and improved operational efficiency.

For Syngenta, the test now shifts from implementation to adoption: whether 10,000 users across 80 countries work faster on the single system, and whether the cleaner data base supports new digital tools for growers. For Infosys, delivery credibility in SAP transformations remains a competitive asset as manufacturers face deadlines to move to S/4HANA.
